ARC-0055.title: A8 (UX / product-first): Where usability fights safety: defaults, one-click install, and approval fatigue
ARC-0055.question_or_target: Where does usability fight safety? Examine default-permissive presets, one-click install of an unreviewed package, and an approval prompt so frequent it trains the owner to accept blindly. Specify which decisions may be DEFAULTED and which must remain explicit, with the rationale for each tied to blast radius rather than to convenience.
ARC-0055.evidence_requirement: The approval-fatigue claim is grounded in a measured prompt rate from real sessions; each defaulted decision states the worst-case outcome if the default is wrong.
tests_required: Blast-radius classification per decision, with the reversal cost stated
Fatigue measurement: prompts per hour in a real session, before and after the proposed defaults
ARC-0055.reviewer_requirement: two reviewers, one of them cross-vendor (Codex), because a same-vendor reviewer shares the author's blind spots
ARC-0055.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot: after two failed attempts on the same framing, enumerate at least two alternative decompositions before a third attempt (AGENTS.md 4b)

ARC-0056.title: A8 (UX / product-first): Preserving owner muscle memory: aliasing, deprecation windows and removal evidence
ARC-0056.question_or_target: Design the migration from today's command surface (slash commands, skills, monitors, ad-hoc scripts) to the product surface WITHOUT breaking the owner's muscle memory: which names are preserved, which are aliased, which are deprecated with a warning period, and what usage evidence must be observed before a deprecated name is actually removed.
ARC-0056.evidence_requirement: The current surface is enumerated mechanically from the live command and skill trees rather than from memory, and every entry receives an explicit disposition.
tests_required: Disposition totality: enumerated names equal preserved plus aliased plus deprecated plus removed, computed
Alias round-trip test: every aliased old name resolves to the new target in a live invocation check
ARC-0056.reviewer_requirement: one independent reviewer must confirm the plan is content-preserving in BOTH directions before it is scored
ARC-0056.retry_policy: re-measure once with a MECHANICALLY DIFFERENT probe (different shell, different data field); if the two readings disagree report BLOCKED with both numbers rather than picking one

ARC-0076.title: Verdict-stability replay: does the winner survive a different panel
ARC-0076.question_or_target: Is the winner a property of the ARCHITECTURES or of the PANEL? Re-run the scoring round with a mechanically different panel (different seat assignment, different vendor mix, different presentation order) and measure whether the winner and the top-three ordering change. Report the stability as a number, and treat an unstable verdict as a finding that must reach the owner before ratification.
ARC-0076.evidence_requirement: The replay is genuinely independent: a different seat roster AND a different entry presentation order, with both differences recorded; re-running the identical configuration would not count as a second signal.
tests_required: Order-effect control: presentation order is permuted and the position bias is measured
Stability metric published: probability the same winner emerges, with the number of replays stated
Both-states control: inject a deliberately weak entry and assert it never wins under any panel
ARC-0076.reviewer_requirement: one non-judge reviewer confirms the replay panel is mechanically different from the original before results are read
ARC-0076.retry_policy: retry ONCE on win-arg-limit with --ignore-user-config and a --prompt-file transport; never --background; on schema-invalid do not retry, fix the schema and re-dispatch
